instructions: Peel the carrots and slice them into 1/4 inch coins. Chop the onion, mince the garlic and grate 2 tbsp of ginger.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Cook the onion about 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the ginger, garlic, cumin and cinnamon and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the carrots, the broth and the salt. Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the carrots are easily pierced with a fork.
Blend until smooth, in batches or with an immersion blender, holding the lid down with a towel. Return the soup to the pot and add a splash of broth or water if it's too thick.
Off the heat, stir in 2 tsp lemon juice and the pepper. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot. For packed lunches, cool the soup and keep it in the fridge up to 4 days or in the freezer up to 3 months. Reheat it with a splash of water until steaming.
method_notes: About 35 minutes. No version found had 20 or more ratings (the best had 3 to 5), so this is a fallback lead: Vegan Family Recipes (5.0 from 3) softens onion, garlic and ginger, simmers carrots in vegetable broth and blends. Strength and Sunshine adds a little cumin, cinnamon and lemon, which are used here, with the lemon stirred in at the end. Ginger is raised to 2 tbsp because the lead's amount is very small for a soup named for it. The Modern Proper version gets its creaminess from coconut milk, which was left out; the carrots blend smooth on their own.
